value.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real normed additive group with Borel measurable space and an additive Haar measure μ. Let F,G,W be real normed additive groups and B:F→L(G,W) a continuous bilinear map. For f:E→F, f′:E→L(E,F), g:E→G, g′:E→L(E,G) and v∈E, if x↦B(f′(x)v,g(x)), x↦B(f(x),g′(x)v), and x↦B(f(x),g(x)) are μ-integrable; f has Frechet derivative f′ on tsupport(g); and g has Frechet derivative g′ on tsupport(f), then ∫B(f(x),g′(x)v)dμ=−∫B(f′(x)v,g(x))dμ.

hypotheses: E has a measurable space, Borel space, finite-dimensional real normed additive structure; μ is an additive Haar measure.
F,G,W have real normed additive structures and B is continuous bilinear.
The three displayed scalar/product functions are μ-integrable.
At every x in tsupport(g), f has Frechet derivative f′(x); at every x in tsupport(f), g has Frechet derivative g′(x).

patches.value: Fix r>0. N001 supplies a compact C and a closed time window containing r in its interior such that u=q outside C throughout that window, with the first time and spatial derivatives supported in C. For every spatial index j, put f(x)=∂_{x_j}u(x,r), g(x)=u_t(x,r), and v equal to the jth Euclidean coordinate vector. Smoothness and constancy of u off C imply f,g and their first Frechet derivatives are continuous and vanish off C; thus the three scalar products B(f′(x)v,g(x)), B(f(x),g′(x)v), B(f(x),g(x)) are continuous and compactly supported. By the ambient Euclidean finite-on-compacts property and M001 they are integrable. The derivative identities hold everywhere by smoothness, hence in particular on the required topological supports. Apply M011 with B the Euclidean inner product to obtain ∫∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t=−∫∂_{x_jx_j}u·u_t. Summing over j and using the finite-dimensional product rule gives ∫e_t=2∫u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu). N002 identifies E′(r) with ∫e_t, yielding the stated formula for arbitrary r>0.

value.bindings: X=ℝⁿ with Borel measurable space and Lebesgue measure, V=ℝ, f equal successively to each of the three scalar product functions formed from u_t, ∂_{x_j}u, and their spatial Frechet derivatives.
hypothesis_checks: The Euclidean measurable and topological structures have measurable opens.
ℝ is a normed additive commutative group.
Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets, established by R002's ambient argument.
Each product is continuous and supported in the compact set C by smoothness and constancy of u outside C.

value.bindings: E=ℝⁿ, μ=Lebesgue/Haar measure, F=G=ℝ^m, W=ℝ, B the Euclidean dot product, f=∂_{x_j}u, g=u_t, v=e_j, f′ and g′ their Frechet derivatives.
hypothesis_checks: ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional over ℝ, Borel, and carries Lebesgue additive Haar measure.
The finite-dimensional real vector spaces are normed additive groups and the Euclidean inner product is continuous bilinear.
Each of B(f′v,g), B(f,g′v), and B(f,g) is continuous with compact support by N001 and smoothness, hence integrable by M001.
Smoothness gives the required Frechet derivative identities everywhere, hence on tsupport(g) and tsupport(f).
